readable_summary:
TEACHER-LOOP SCALING (single-seed smoke, cupy/RTX-3090, 2026-08-08). Reuses the corrective-acquisition e-prop path (OnBridgeEpropNet FF weights moved by the brain's OWN transport-free e-prop rule; NO host store-write). N distinct referent->patient facts taught SEQUENTIALLY into ONE brain.

MEASURED:
  * Throughput: 88.6 s/fact mean over 39 facts (median 87.6, range 84.9-104.1) in the full N=40 run; 88.4 s/fact over 10 facts in the focused run. Per-fact cost is ~flat in N (readout width fixed at build).
  * Immediate acquisition: 0.995 mean (min 0.95) over 39 facts, chance 0.025 -- the brain learns EVERY fact essentially perfectly the moment it is taught. The mechanism is NOT the limiter.
  * Retention curve (sequential, re-test all earlier facts after teaching N): N=1 -> 1/1 (mean 1.00); N=5 -> 3/5 (mean 0.40); N=10 -> 1/10 (mean 0.13); N=20 -> 1/20 (mean 0.077). Fact 0 reads 0.00 from N>=5 on. frac_recalled ~ 1/N: only the ~1 most-recent fact survives.
  * CRUX (same net, same capacity, same per-fact epoch budget): SEQUENTIAL N=10 retains 1/10 (0.10=chance); INTERLEAVED N=10 retains 8/10 (0.66). Interleaving keeps 6.6x more. The net CAN hold ~8-10 facts; the sequential single-fact corrective updates DESTROY earlier ones.

WHAT SETS THE PACE: catastrophic forgetting, decisively. Throughput is fast, acquisition is perfect, capacity is adequate (interleaved 8/10) -- yet sequential retention collapses to ~1 fact. Breadth is blocked by interference on the shared readout, NOT by throughput and NOT by a mechanism/capacity wall.

EXTRAPOLATION to 1000 facts: throughput MEASURED 88.5 s/fact x 1000 EXTRAPOLATED = 88,500 s = 24.6 h (~1.02 days) on the 3090 -- NOT months. BUT retention EXTRAPOLATED from the ~1/N curve => ~1-3 facts retained at N=1000. So the 1-day figure counts facts PRESENTED, not RETAINED. A forgetting-mitigation mechanism (sleep-replay consolidation / interleaved rehearsal / sparse-gated readout allocation / protected per-fact subspaces) is a PREREQUISITE before 1000 RETAINED facts is reachable at all. (Epochs=60 is also overkill -- immediate acquisition is already 1.0 -- so ~10 epochs would cut per-fact to ~15 s => ~4 h/1000; moot until forgetting is solved.)

3090 vs AWS: (1) Per-fact throughput is dominated by 25 sequential Izhikevich settle-steps + per-step host<->device to_host transfers + host-side numpy e-prop grad on a TINY net (46 neurons, 453 synapses). This is latency/overhead-bound, NOT FLOP-bound, so a bigger AWS GPU (A100/H100) gives ~1x (negligible) per-fact speedup -- there are no large matmuls to accelerate. (2) The curriculum is SEQUENTIAL (fact i+1 depends on the brain state after fact i), so cloud PARALLELISM gives ZERO teaching speedup: 100 GPUs teach 1000 facts no faster than 1. Cloud's real value here is parallel INDEPENDENT de-risk EXPERIMENTS (6-seed validation, config sweeps, forgetting-mitigation-mechanism variants), never the one brain's one-fact-after-another schedule.

HONEST CAVEATS: single seed; smoke-scale (N<=40, hidden=24, K<=40); acquire/retention read via the net's argmax (the brain's own e-prop read path), threshold recall = acc>=max(0.5, chance+0.15); readout-norm (leaky-readout homeostatic input scaling) fit ONCE over the whole referent world before the curriculum (an instrument choice -- refitting per-fact would itself distort earlier facts); the full N=40 sequential run was killed at fact 39/40 so N=40 + full-run interleaved were reconstructed from log (throughput + retention N=1/5/10/20 measured); interleaved 8/10 (not 10/10) at 60 epochs hints at a small residual capacity/undertraining component under the dominant forgetting effect.

extrapolation_1000_facts.label: per-fact MEASURED on 3090; x1000 EXTRAPOLATED (sequential, no parallel speedup)
extrapolation_1000_facts.months_framing_verdict: FALSE -- throughput says ~1 day/1000, not months. But breadth is blocked by catastrophic forgetting until a consolidation/rehearsal/allocation mechanism is added; it is a mechanism-prerequisite problem, not a throughput problem.

what_sets_the_pace: CATASTROPHIC FORGETTING (decisive: interleaved 8/10 vs sequential 1/10, same net).
